answer: A textile exchange facing a tide of fake agents selling velvet in sable shades could make each registered key retain a different 5 GB block of random data. A verifier assigns the block, commits its hash and sends unpredictable spot checks with a short deadline; failed checks revoke bidding access. Blocks must not overlap across keys, so aliases cannot all prove possession of one shared copy. Running a thousand accounts then requires roughly 5 TB of storage and timely responses. This raises the cost of a farm, though cheap rented storage can weaken the barrier.
